newsitem.title: THAILAND: Death toll rises to at least 19 in Thai hotel fire.
newsitem.headline: Death toll rises to at least 19 in Thai hotel fire.

text.p: At least 19 people were killed and up to 50 others, including foreign tourists, were injured in a hotel fire in Thailand's eastern beach resort town of Pattaya, government and hospital sources said on Friday.
At least 18 people had been found dead from smoke inhalation inside the Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel, about 200 km (120 miles) southeast of Bangkok, the city's mayor said.
"Eighteen bodies were found trapped in the corridor linking the restaurant and the lobby," Pairat Suthidamgong told reporters. Their nationalities were not known but most were thought to be Thai.

Fire-fighters told Reuters by telephone that the fire broke out in the ground floor coffee house of the Royal Jomtien Resort and then spread from the sixth floor to the 12th floor of the 16-storey building.
Earlier, rescue workers and police said one man jumped from the 11th floor to his death while a man and a woman were burnt to death.
It was not clear if the man and the woman who were burned to death were included in the count given by Pairat.
The number of dead and injured was expected to rise because many people were apparently trapped inside the building, police said.
More than 300 people, mostly Thais attending seminars, were in the hotel at the time the fire broke out.

As thick smoke billowed into the air, several people could be seen trapped on the top floor. Three helicopters were aiding firefighters and airlifting people to safety, live television broadcasts showed.
Some of the injured were rushed to a nearby hospital with serious burns, hospital sources said.
